parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a national document/entry regime engineered against trans people with a division ranked in the harshest-law category. Universal exposures: visa refusal on any sex doubt with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility (foreign detentions triggered eight governments' advisories), passport marker restrictions upheld by the Supreme Court, airport screening outing, government-facility exclusion by birth sex, division school-facility bans, a statutory religious-refusal basis for service denial, and no state non-discrimination or state hate-crime cover for gender identity. Federal custody shows conversion-therapy policy and documented immigration-custody abuse of trans men; a minor traveller faces the state care ban. Offsetting: violence sits near the general homicide baseline, a bias murder drew 49 years, majority public opinion supports protections, litigation is active. Not imprisonment-likely, but no working remedy for the border and facility exposures → Elevated Risk, lower half.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable orders refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and directs officers to weigh permanent fraud ineligibility; X markers ended for new issues; scanners and secondary screening routinely out. Foreign-citizen detentions prompted eight governments' travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, limited waivers exist; existing X passports valid until expiry; ACLU suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Division's March 2026 licence-bar and dual-listed birth certificates do not govern foreign passports but signal official skepticism; document mismatch can escalate to detention then birth-sex placement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented arrest (elsewhere) under a bathroom law with 24 hours in a men's ward; federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies and stopped counting trans prisoners; trans men in immigration custody reported forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse; name changes barred in state custody.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute and 2020 employment ruling operate; a bias murder drew 49 years; no documented adult arrest under the division's own 2024 provision.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A state trespass stop can escalate into federal custody where the documented abuse records sit; rule of law enforces hostile policy efficiently here.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; division 2024 law requires birth-sex bathrooms in public schools and equality maps count 2024-25 bans; four states criminalize in limited circumstances; division has no gender-identity non-discrimination law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states plus capital have no mapped ban; division's broader 2024 bills died; national equality maps and litigation ongoing.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Hospital or shelter placement by document sex is not documented; visitor entering government buildings or campuses carries the exclusion.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care under 18; largest public hospital's adolescent clinic closed; a 2017 religious-liberties statute gives individuals and businesses a statutory basis to refuse service on birth-sex beliefs; national funding freezes and proposed insurance bars.
care_services.protection: Adult care not banned in division; one LGBTQ clinic operates; national employment and hate-crime protections remain; orders partly enjoined.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor can be denied care outright; an adult visitor can be refused by providers citing the state statute with no state recourse.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Justice department reward memo pairs 'radical gender ideology' with violent extremism; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for prioritization; hospital records subpoenaed; executive orders call minor care 'mutilation'; state supreme court called a trans boy 'minor female'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target people who merely disagree; several orders blocked or enjoined; reward criteria never list gender ideology.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both outing probability and severity when police or courts engage a trans visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: State care ban (2023); 2025 high court denied a trans teen's name change citing public policy; sports statute requires genital/DNA/hormone verification; national order directs criminal investigation of teachers supporting social transition; school facility bans by birth sex.
minors_guardians.protection: Parental consent was considered; litigation continues; several national orders enjoined; account of the name-change holding conflicts and is unresolved.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a minor faces care denial, birth-sex facilities, and potential scrutiny of the child's documents; a minor alone has no state-facing protection.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 6.6 trans-women killings per 100k (2008-2025, undercount-adjusted) versus 6.0 general homicide — near-background, not a campaign; 2017 bias murder documented in division; state hate-crime law omits gender identity; only four municipalities bar discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National prosecution secured 49 years; no documented trans killing in division since 2017; 67-68% back non-discrimination; pride parade drew 3,000; federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Baseline violence plus statutory service-refusal means recourse depends on federal, not state, machinery.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state non-discrimination law; state hate-crime statute excludes gender identity; national orders and passport suit unresolved; no enforcement data on division facility bans against adults; March 2026 licence law's scope and treatment of out-of-state licences unsourced; no recent trans-resident experience survey.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal courts have granted injunctions; ACLU suit, legal-aid FAQ, municipal ordinances in four cities; national employment protection operates.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions cluster exactly where a visitor would need them answered — documents, detention placement, service refusal.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars transgender visitors outright through a register with near-nil appeal. Here refusal is discretionary, tied to documented sex doubt, requires a four-element fraud finding, and is contested in court with legal aid available. Border severity is comparable, but functioning remedies and no universal entry ban put this above 0.35-A.

Kestrel Isles shows secondary screening, discretionary refusal, slow administrative appeal, and humiliation — no facility regime, no custody abuse, no statutory service-refusal. This dossier adds a possible lifetime fraud bar, documented foreign detentions, government-facility exclusion, custody-conversion policy and a hostile state supreme court: materially lower than 0.55-B.

Meridia has trained border staff, tribunal appeals, compensation for unlawful holding, and respectful inspection norms. This regime lacks every one of those: officers are directed toward refusal and fraud referral, facility exclusion is state policy, and state recourse is absent. Far below 0.75-C.

Drellia's durable daily exposure via registration and hotel databases, with criminal charges uncommon and an ombudsman that rarely disciplines, resembles this dossier's universal document friction and thin state remedy. This case is slightly lower: custody abuse is documented, an arrest has occurred somewhere nationally, and a lifetime immigration bar is in play.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: national document and entry rules that treat sex doubt as a refusal ground (with lifetime fraud exposure and documented foreign detentions), layered on a division that bans birth-sex facility use, bans minor care, denies name changes, and offers no state non-discrimination or hate-crime cover. Institutional efficiency cuts both ways — courts convicted a bias killer to 49 years and enjoined some orders, but also upheld passport restrictions and called a trans teen 'minor female.' Violence sits near the general homicide baseline, so severity, not street lethality, drives the score: universal border exposure, facility exclusion with one documented arrest nationally, statutory service refusal, and federal custody abuse with no working state remedy. Litigation and majority public support hold it above the 0.35 tier; absent demonstrated remedies it stays in Elevated Risk's lower half.
